I need to find the characteristic polynomial of the matrix $A$ by computing $\det(A - \lambda I)$.

$$A - \lambda I = \left(\begin{array}{ccc} -4-\lambda & -13 & 10 \\ -9 & 10-\lambda & 4 \\ 12 & -5 & -14-\lambda \end{array}\right)$$

I'll compute the determinant by expanding along the first row:

$$\det(A - \lambda I) = (-4-\lambda)\det\left(\begin{array}{cc} 10-\lambda & 4 \\ -5 & -14-\lambda \end{array}\right) - (-13)\det\left(\begin{array}{cc} -9 & 4 \\ 12 & -14-\lambda \end{array}\right) + 10\det\left(\begin{array}{cc} -9 & 10-\lambda \\ 12 & -5 \end{array}\right)$$

**First minor:**
$(10-\lambda)(-14-\lambda) - (4)(-5) = -140 - 10\lambda + 14\lambda + \lambda^2 + 20 = \lambda^2 + 4\lambda - 120$

**Second minor:**
$(-9)(-14-\lambda) - (4)(12) = 126 + 9\lambda - 48 = 9\lambda + 78$

**Third minor:**
$(-9)(-5) - (10-\lambda)(12) = 45 - 120 + 12\lambda = 12\lambda - 75$

**Putting it together:**

$$\det(A - \lambda I) = (-4-\lambda)(\lambda^2 + 4\lambda - 120) + 13(9\lambda + 78) + 10(12\lambda - 75)$$

**First term:**
$(-4-\lambda)(\lambda^2 + 4\lambda - 120)$
$= -4\lambda^2 - 16\lambda + 480 - \lambda^3 - 4\lambda^2 + 120\lambda$
$= -\lambda^3 - 8\lambda^2 + 104\lambda + 480$

**Second term:**
$13(9\lambda + 78) = 117\lambda + 1014$

**Third term:**
$10(12\lambda - 75) = 120\lambda - 750$

**Sum:**
$-\lambda^3 - 8\lambda^2 + 104\lambda + 480 + 117\lambda + 1014 + 120\lambda - 750$

$= -\lambda^3 - 8\lambda^2 + (104 + 117 + 120)\lambda + (480 + 1014 - 750)$

$= -\lambda^3 - 8\lambda^2 + 341\lambda + 744$

The characteristic polynomial is typically written with leading coefficient positive, so:

$$\boxed{\lambda^3 + 8\lambda^2 - 341\lambda - 744}$$
